citations.narrative:
One (1) adult rabbit was housed in the aviary, in the same primary enclosure as the birds. The rabbit appeared to be in
good condition, and while the enclosure provided sufficient space, shelter, and access to food and water, rabbits are a
species that are not permitted to be co-housed with any other species, unless for specific scientific purposes. Housing
rabbits with other species may result in injury or compatibility issues. Correct by ensuring all rabbits shall not be housed in
the same primary enclosure with any other species of animals.
Correct by: Oct. 23, 2026.

The facility does not have a 6 ft perimeter fence around the enclosure containing three (3) red kangaroos. The south side
of the enclosure is bordered by the road providing access to the customer train and a second road that provides access
for deliveries. The access to these roads is closed by two (2) gates when the facility is closed to the public. Between the
gates and along that side of the property, there are ditches and an overgrown natural barrier that does provide sight and
access limitations to the paved road along that side. The west side is bordered by the public access to the adventure
park. The north and east sides are bordered by natural vegetation and agriculture fields. There is also a Great Pyrenees
protection dog that lives with the kangaroos.
An inadequate perimeter fence leaves the facility vulnerable, creating opportunities for intruders or wild animals to enter
and potentially compromises the safety and well-being of the animals.
All outdoor housing facilities must be enclosed by a perimeter fence that is of sufficient height to keep animals and
unauthorized persons out. The fence must be constructed so that it protects the animals in the facility by restricting
animals and unauthorized persons from going through it or under it and having contact with the animals in the facility, and
so that it can function as a secondary containment system for the animals in the facility. The perimeter fence must be
sufficient distance from the outside of the primary enclosure to prevent physical contact between animals inside the
enclosure and animals or persons outside the perimeter fence. Non-dangerous animals housed in outdoor facilities
require a 6-foot-tall perimeter fence around their enclosure and must be at least 3 feet away from any enclosures or
buildings, unless an approved variance has been issued in writing by the Administrator.
Correct by: Nov. 20, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
